title: In a Back Alley
text: I arrived at a village near Melromarc’s castle town via the portal. Since this was the exact location I’d registered, I’m heading straight for the castle town on foot.
Huh? The village near the castle town… was it Riyute Village? Well, it’s in ruins now.

Charred buildings, pastures ravaged by monsters… the remains of houses that have been gnawed away, and destroyed dwellings. It seems to have lost all resemblance to a village. Temporary tents have been set up, but the villagers look gloomy. Well, there’s no need for me to go inside, so I’ll just pass by.

But… come to think of it, waves do occur near the castle. Hmm… as I try to recall, was the damage really this severe? I seem to remember the village retaining its appearance a bit better—or am I mistaken? Or perhaps it’s because fewer heroes participated in the Melromarc wave?

There’s no point in worrying about it. I left the gloomy village behind and headed toward the castle town. All right, then! My goal for today is to find Filo-tan at the Monster Merchant’s tent. I’ve got plenty of money. I came here intending to buy up every single one of Filolial-sama’s eggs in that tent.

I skip past the shops in the castle town. Hmm… some of them are closed. The apothecary and the Magic Shop are shut. Well, they’re shops I have absolutely no need to visit anyway. I continue down the back alleys toward the Monster Merchant’s tent.
“W-wait, you’re Motoyasu!?”

Would you believe it? While walking through the back alleys, I somehow ran into Ren. Hmm… what should I do? If I kill him too easily, I’ll just end up in a loop. But if he makes a fuss, it’ll be noisy. Alright, then I’ll just silence him enough so he doesn’t die.
“W-wait! I have no intention of fighting you, and I don’t plan on causing a scene here!”

Just as I try to grip my spear tightly, Ren holds out his hand to restrain me. Hmm, that’s a surprisingly virtuous attitude for Ren these days. If Ren has no hostile intentions, it might be wise to at least have a chat. He might have some useful information. Or perhaps he’s just buying time while he prepares to fight.
“What’s gotten into you all of a sudden?”
“It’s nothing like that—I have no intention of fighting. More importantly, why is Motoyasu here? Didn’t you go to Siltvelt?”
“It’s obvious—because Filo-tan is here, isn’t it?”
“H-huh… I don’t really get it, but why don’t we talk for a bit?”
“You’re just saying that so you can call the castle guards, aren’t you!”
“That’s why I told you to listen! I have no intention of calling them.”

Hmm… I just can’t seem to trust him. Come to think of it, it’s best to eliminate any potential threats before they become a problem. I’ve already escorted my father to Siltvelt, so I suppose the Three Heroes Church—who tried to take his life—will have to face the consequences.
“If you like, right here or anywhere else—anywhere Motoyasu chooses—just hear me out for a bit.”
“Understood. So? What’s this about?”
“Is it okay to talk here…? Well, there’s a lot to cover. I’d also like you to pass this along to Naofumi—about what’s going on in this country.”
Ren started talking to me. Apparently, after I went after my Father, Melromarc treated Ren and Itsuki very well.

Then, using the aid money as capital, Ren bought equipment and went to level up to become stronger. During that time, he heard rumors about us, but he says he was more interested in testing how quickly he could get stronger using the knowledge he already had. Well, things were going smoothly up to that point, apparently.

However, according to Ren… lately, a sense of unease has started to take hold. He told me that one of Itsuki’s companions was lynched and killed by Demi-Humans who call themselves the “Shield Sect” and worship my Father.

Ren had been gathering evidence, but something seemed off. For one thing, since my Father and his group were on their way to Siltvelt, he couldn’t understand why they’d be targeting the Hero’s life on Father’s orders. That’s what Ren told me.
“So, Motoyasu. I’ve been wondering… did Naofumi really try to harm us? Motoyasu, did you come here to kill us?”
“Not at all. The only reason I came to Melromarc this time was to buy Filo-tan.”
“…Well, if killing us were the goal, he’d have done it already.”

Ren seemed to have convinced himself of that on his own. Exactly. Killing Ren or Itsuki would serve no purpose. In fact, it would render everything we’ve done so far meaningless. If anyone’s worth killing, it’s Trash and the Pope.
“Let’s continue. Something’s definitely off about this country. I get the feeling that Itsuki has been getting more and more cocky ever since the princess took a liking to him.”
“Is that so?”

“Yeah, the king and princess are pretty suspicious. When I confronted them about Motoyasu being trapped on the first day, they put on a phony act, saying something like, ‘We’ve caused a misunderstanding. The entire nation will come to his aid,’ but in the end, we were forced to break through the border, right?　Even if we assume the ‘forced breakthrough’ was a misunderstanding despite them saying they’d cooperate… that’s a contradiction, isn’t it?”
It seems Ren actually believed the story I told him.

“To top it all off… last night, after we defeated the Wave Boss and attended the party at the castle, do you know what they told us? ‘It seems you heroes still lack training; please continue to improve,’ they said!”
Ren seems to be venting—maybe he’s been bottling up some stress. But since I can get all sorts of information from him, I’ll just nod along.

“When I asked why our training wasn’t sufficient, they said, ‘The Heroes of Legend are much stronger. Please master god-like strength.’ It felt like they were judging us based on rumors—like the one about Motoyasu blowing up a fortress—and it was really annoying.”
“That’s no lie. A fortress of that caliber? It took just one blow.”
“…I know the rumors have been exaggerated.”
It seems Ren doesn’t quite grasp just how strong a Hero is. Well, just like I was in the first world, Ren and the others didn’t believe what Father said at first, either.
“He did give me some financial aid, but I’m planning to seek asylum in Zeltoble… or rather, go into hiding. If anything happens, look for me in Zeltoble. See ya.”
With that, Ren says what he needs to say and tries to leave. But halfway out, he turns back.
“Motoyasu! Watch out for Melromarc! There’s something fishy going on!”
He leaves those words behind and runs off. He’s probably heading to Zeltoble through the back alleys now.

Zeltoble, huh? Well, that country is perfect for hiding out. The crime rate’s a bit high, but with the Dragon Hourglass there, it shouldn’t be a bad place. More importantly, my top priority is to buy Filo-tan.
“Well, well, a new customer? Hello.”
“This time, it’s definitely Filo-tan.”
“Huh?”
As I stepped into the tent, a familiar monster merchant greeted me.
“Filo-tan.”
“Huh? Um…”
The monster merchant was staring at me from head to toe. Then, he started to panic as if he’d suddenly broken out in a cold sweat.
“Uh, um. I believe that figure of yours is the one rumored to be the Spear Hero. Yes.”
“That’s right! I’m Motoyasu Kitamura, the Spear Hero!”
For some reason, the monster merchant suddenly stumbled and nearly fell.
“W-well… what brings the Spear Hero—who’s wanted in Melromarc as the mastermind behind the fortress destruction—here, sir?”
Wanted? Ah, that must be from when I turned the tables on my Father after he tried to unleash Ceremonial Magic on me. But I was just fending off a threat that came my way.

Besides, even if I were wanted, neither the townspeople nor the passersby showed any reaction at all. People don’t really pay attention to faces as much as you’d think. They seem to make allowances based on how similar I look to the wanted poster. They probably didn’t expect a wanted criminal to be walking through town in broad daylight.
“I’ve come to buy Filo-tan.”
Today is the day after the Melromarc Wave, so working backward, this must be the day my Father purchased Filo-tan. Therefore, Filo-tan should be here today.
“Filo-tan is…”
Just as he was about to say that, the monster merchant’s subordinate next to him whispered something to him. After nodding a few times, the monster merchant asked me:
“By ‘Filo-tan,’ do you mean a Filolial?”
“That’s right. Or are you saying you won’t sell to me?”
I gripped my spear firmly to show him. It’s a negotiation technique my Father taught me.
“O-okay, I understand. Yes. Over here…”
“I’ll buy every single Filolial Aria-species egg in this tent.”
